comparisons.peer_topic: Stock Repurchase Program Activity and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's authorized $12 billion stock repurchase program saw the company repurchase 5.9 million shares for $862 million during the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024, with $4.7 billion remaining as of that date. The program has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time without obligation to acquire any specific amount of stock.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose active stock repurchase programs under Item 8. AVGO explicitly states that it fully utilized the $20 billion of authorized repurchase amounts prior to the December 31, 2023 expiration, with $7,176 million spent in fiscal year 2024. In contrast, AMD’s $12 billion program has no termination date; as of its fiscal year-end, $4.7 billion remained available, and the company repurchased $862 million in shares during the year. While both companies utilize share repurchases, AVGO had exhausted its specific historical authorization buckets, whereas AMD continues to have significant remaining authority under an open-ended program.

sentences.text: All $20 billion of the authorized amount under these stock repurchase programs was utilized prior to expiration on December 31, 2023.

During fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022, we repurchased and retired approximately 67 million, 91 million and 117 million shares of our common stock for $7,176 million, $5,824 million and $7,000 million, respectively.
This Repurchase Program does not obligate the Company to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under this program.

comparisons.peer_summary: Employees purchased 39 million shares for $972 million in 2024, a decrease from 43 million shares ($1.0 billion) in 2023 and 27 million shares ($931 million) in 2022. Unrecognized compensation costs for these rights totaled $63 million as of December 28, 2024, to be recognized over approximately two months.

comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU disclose discretionary stock repurchase programs authorized by their Boards of Directors. MU has a $10 billion authorization with no expiration date, spending $300 million in 2024 and having repurchased an aggregate of $7.19 billion through August 2024. Both companies cite the repurchases as discretionary and subject to market conditions and cash needs, though AVGO’s historical authorization was finite while MU’s is indefinite.

sentences.text: In December 2021, our Board of Directors authorized a stock repurchase program to repurchase up to $10 billion of our common stock from time to time through December 31, 2022, which was subsequently extended to December 31, 2023.

During fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022, we repurchased and retired approximately 67 million, 91 million and 117 million shares of our common stock for $7,176 million, $5,824 million and $7,000 million, respectively.

Our Board of Directors has authorized the discretionary repurchase of up to $10 billion of our outstanding common stock through open-market purchases, block trades, privately-negotiated transactions, derivative transactions, and/or pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 trading plans.

comparisons.peer_topic: Share Repurchase Program Authorization and Activity
comparisons.peer_summary: In August 2023, the Board authorized an additional $25.0 billion for share repurchases without expiration, with $9.7 billion spent in fiscal 2024 and $1.9 billion in early 2024. As of January 28, 2024, $22.5 billion remained authorized, and the program aims to offset employee dilution while remaining subject to market conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA disclose significant stock repurchase programs aimed at offsetting dilution and managing capital. AVGO utilized $7,176 million in FY2024 to exhaust its $20 billion authorization. NVDA repurchased $9.7 billion in FY2024 under a program that was increased by $25 billion in August 2023, leaving $22.5 billion authorized as of its fiscal year-end. Both companies explicitly state their repurchase programs are discretionary, have no expiration (NVDA's current one; AVGO's new authority is implied as previous expired but activity continues), and are subject to market conditions.
